headline: mbillow/localthings
abstract: Control your Samsung appliances from Home Assistant over your home network, with no cloud account. LocalThings Control your Samsung appliances from Home Assistant over your home network, with no cloud account. LocalThings connects Home Assistant to Samsung washers, dryers, refrigerators, air conditioners, ovens and other appliances that work with the SmartThings app. It talks to each appliance on your local network. Updates are fast. Appliances that support push send changes as they happen. LocalThings checks the rest every 30 seconds. It works without the internet. After setup, LocalThings never contacts Samsung's servers. Your data stays home. LocalThings sends nothing to Samsung. The appliance itself still keeps its own connection to Samsung, and LocalThings doesn't change that. Setup needs an IP address. For most appliances, you enter the address and LocalThings works out the type and model, then creates matching controls and sensors. This sounds extreme and I wouldn’t have believed it even a year ago, but we’re starting to see plenty of examples of productivity gains that are an order of magnitude or two above output levels pre-AI. With the right harness, a deep understanding of your domain of what you want to build, likely a relatively new codebase (with some exceptions), a fluency of how to work with multiple agents at once, and a setup that makes it so you can test and deploy with limited friction, outputs on this level feel realistic in coding. What’s crazy is this gap doesn’t appear to be diminishing over time. You’d think that we’d see a convergence in the lines because of AI, but it turns out the more depth you had before -and willingness now to take a different approach- gives you crazy leverage. And that is only compounding as the models can take on larger work and harder problems. Right now this is most pronounced in software engineering for the obvious reasons. But there’s no reason we don’t start to see this in a number of other computer-use-sensitive domains like other scientific fields, AEC, finance, cyber, and more. Going to get quite wild.
